*Note: In the U.S. measuring systems the same word may have two meanings. For example, an ounce may mean 1/16 of a pound and 1/16 of a pint; but 
the former is strictly a weight measure, and the latter is a volume measure. Except in the case of water, milk, or other liquids of the same density, a fluid 
ounce and an ounce of weight are two completely different quantities. These measures are not to be used interchangeably.
